english: He talks as if he knew everything.
tip: Come se (as if) always takes the subjunctive: come se sapesse = as if he knew.

english: If he had more courage, he'd speak up.
tip: In hypotheticals, se + past subjunctive (avesse) pairs with the conditional in the main clause (parlerebbe).

target: La settimana scorsa ho lavorato tanto.
english: Last week I worked a lot.
tip: Most verbs take the helper verb avere in the past: ho lavorato = I worked. Movement verbs switch to essere: sono andato.

target: Perfetto, allora ci vediamo alle otto.
english: Perfect, then we'll see each other at eight.
tip: In ci vediamo, ci means each other: we see each other. Ci can also mean us, there, or about it depending on context.

target: Poco fa ho ricevuto una chiamata.
english: A little while ago I received a call.
tip: After a time phrase, fa means ago: poco fa = a little while ago.

target: Forse dovremmo partire più presto domani.
english: Maybe we should leave earlier tomorrow.
tip: Forse (maybe) keeps the normal indicative or conditional, no subjunctive: forse dovremmo partire = maybe we should leave.

target: Davvero è successo tutto così velocemente?
english: Really, did it all happen so quickly?
tip: Add -mente to an adjective to build an adverb: veloce becomes velocemente = quickly.

target: Ho visto tua sorella al supermercato.
english: I saw your sister at the supermarket.
tip: Drop the article with a possessive before one singular family member: tua sorella = your sister.

target: Quando ho aperto la porta, dormivano tutti.
english: When I opened the door, everyone was sleeping.
tip: Passato prossimo (ho aperto) for single action + imperfetto (dormivano) for state.

target: Era molto tardi e ho preso un taxi.
english: It was very late and I took a taxi.
tip: Prendere has the irregular past participle preso, so the passato prossimo is ho preso.
'a casa' means home or at home, with no article: Vai a casa.
Polite commands to someone you address as Lei use the subjunctive form: si preoccupi, not preoccupati.
Italian 'has' fear rather than 'is' scared: avere paura = to be scared.
For -ere and -ire verbs, the informal tu command is just the present-tense form: Leggi.
A past yes/no question changes only intonation, with no helper like English 'did': Hai incontrato Marco?
divertirsi is reflexive, literally to enjoy oneself: Ti sei divertita? = Did you have fun?
Getting angry is reflexive in Italian: arrabbiarsi. Ti sei arrabbiata? = Did you get angry?
Passing an exam uses superare, not passare: ha superato l'esame.
arrivare forms the past with essere, so the participle agrees: sei arrivato (m), arrivata (f).
Here 'ci' stands in for 'about it': Ci pensi bene = think it over.
A break is something you 'make' in Italian: fare una pausa.
sbagliare means to get something wrong: hai sbagliato numero = you dialed the wrong number.
The noi form doubles as English 'let's': parliamo means both 'we talk' and 'let's talk'.
Use giocare a before games and sports: giocare a carte.
Before lo or la, the pronoun ti becomes te: te l'ha detto = told it to you.
To need is 'to have need of': avere bisogno di aiuto.
Subject pronouns are usually dropped, since mando already means I send; Io here adds emphasis.
guardare already means to look at, so no preposition follows: abbiamo guardato un film.
'A' contracts with articles: al (a+il), alla (a+la), ai (a+i), alle (a+le). Mandatory with definite articles.
entrare needs 'in' before a place: sono entrati nel museo (in + il = nel).
